rationale: Revision of the pooled Gaussian prototype mechanism: allow each cultivar its own chemical spread. Support shows cultivar 2 has broader phenolic, ash, hue, and magnesium distributions, cultivar 1 has broader proline, and cultivar 3 has broader color intensity. Shared variance incorrectly treats rare high-magnesium/high-phenolic cultivar 2 wines as ever-stronger evidence for cultivar 1, matching the development error pattern. Class-conditional variances are 70% empirical variance and 30% pooled within-class variance, followed by 10% shrinkage toward unit standardized variance. Class means, prior counts, 1.25 temperature, and phenolic redundancy weights match candidate 1. The Gaussian log likelihood is expanded into per-coordinate quadratic, linear, and constant terms. A 247-unit ReLU hidden layer represents 13 independent squares via half-unit linear interpolation on [-4.5,4.5] (linear tails), plus signed identity units. This approximates the quadratic likelihood without training. Missing indicators are unused. All parameters come only from support counts, means and variances.
